evidence.title: Robert Weber Round Barn
evidence.text: The Robert Weber Round Barn is a round barn located east of Durand, Illinois, United States along Illinois Route 75 in Harrison Township.

evidence.title: Robert Weber Round Barn
evidence.text: The Weber barn was constructed in 1917 and features a roof designed and built by the Haas Brothers, who worked on other area round barns.

evidence.title: Robert Weber Round Barn
evidence.text: The barn is 55 ft in diameter and features a 24 ft diameter central silo.

evidence.title: Robert Weber Round Barn
evidence.text: The design of the Weber Round Barn stands out from other area round barns in its vitrified tile walls, a development used in later period American round barns.

evidence.title: Robert Weber Round Barn
evidence.text: The Robert Weber Round Barn was added to the U.S. National Register of Historic Places in 1984.

evidence.title: Kent Dairy Round Barn
evidence.text: The Kent Dairy Round Barn near Red Lodge, Montana is a round barn that was built during 1939-1941 and is believed to be one of the last round dairy barns built in the United States.

evidence.title: Kent Dairy Round Barn
evidence.text: It has an adjoining rectangular milkhouse.

evidence.title: Kent Dairy Round Barn
evidence.text: The barn was built under supervision of master barn builder, Emery McNamee, by Ephraim Kent and sons Armas, Harry, James, Leo, and Waino.

evidence.title: James Bruce Round Barn
evidence.text: The James Bruce Round Barn is a round barn located near the Stephenson County, Illinois city of Freeport, United States.

evidence.title: James Bruce Round Barn
evidence.text: The barn was constructed in 1914 by the team of Jeremiah Shaffer and the Haas Brothers, who were responsible for at least a dozen round barns in the area.

evidence.title: James Bruce Round Barn
evidence.text: The barn features a single hip roof design which was probably influenced by the Agricultural Experiment Stations at the University of Illinois and the University of Wisconsin–Madison.

evidence.title: James Bruce Round Barn
evidence.text: The Bruce Round Barn was the last known round barn designed by the Shaffer–Haas team.

evidence.title: James Bruce Round Barn
evidence.text: The building was listed on the U.S. National Register of Historic Places as part of a multiple property submission in 1984.

evidence.title: Virginia Tillery Round Barn
evidence.text: The Virginia Tillery Round Barn is a round barn located on County Route 738 west of White Hall in Greene County, Illinois.

evidence.title: Virginia Tillery Round Barn
evidence.text: The barn was built in the fall of 1912 for farmer Harry C. Price.

evidence.title: Virginia Tillery Round Barn
evidence.text: With a 36 ft diameter, the barn is relatively small for an Illinois round barn; the median diameter of Illinois round barns was 60 ft .

evidence.title: Virginia Tillery Round Barn
evidence.text: Its size suggests that it served as a general-purpose barn, not a dairy barn like the state's larger round barns.

evidence.title: Virginia Tillery Round Barn
evidence.text: Brown tile blocks were used to build the barn, which is topped by a wood shingle roof with a cupola.

evidence.title: Dennis Otte Round Barn
evidence.text: The Dennis Otte Round Barn is a round barn in the U.S. state of Illinois near the unincorporated Stephenson County community of Eleroy.

evidence.title: Dennis Otte Round Barn
evidence.text: The barn was built in 1930 by Herman Altenbern and has a diameter of 54 feet (16.5 m).

evidence.title: Dennis Otte Round Barn
evidence.text: The barn is representative of the last round barn design variations that evolved.

evidence.title: Dennis Otte Round Barn
evidence.text: The Otte Round Barn was added to the U.S. National Register of Historic Places in 1984.

evidence.title: Bert Leedy Round Barn
evidence.text: The Bert Leedy Round Barn, also known as Paxton Round Barn and as Fulton County Historical Society Round Barn, is a round barn located in Richland Township near Rochester, Indiana, United States.

evidence.title: Bert Leedy Round Barn
evidence.text: Built in 1924, it was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1993.

evidence.title: Bert Leedy Round Barn
evidence.text: The listing was consistent with terms of a National Park Service "Multiple Property Documentation" study on "Round and Polygonal Barns of Indiana" that was prepared in 1991.

evidence.title: Bert Leedy Round Barn
evidence.text: The Round Barn was moved to its current site, an open-air museum, in 1989 after it was struck by a tornado.

evidence.title: Thomas Ranck Round Barn
evidence.text: The Thomas Ranck Round Barn is a round barn in Waterloo Township near the Fayette-Wayne County, Indiana county line.

evidence.title: Thomas Ranck Round Barn
evidence.text: It is one of many round barns built in Indiana during the late 19th and early 20th centuries.

evidence.title: Thomas Ranck Round Barn
evidence.text: Of the round barns built in eastern Indiana during this period the Ranck Round Barn stands out as one of the most elaborately designed structures.

evidence.title: Thomas Ranck Round Barn
evidence.text: The Thomas Ranck Round Barn was listed on the U.S. National Register of Historic Places in January 1983.

evidence.title: University of Illinois round barns
evidence.text: The three University of Illinois round barns played a special role in the promotion and popularity of the American round barn.

evidence.title: University of Illinois round barns
evidence.text: They are located in the U.S. city of Urbana, Illinois on the campus of the University of Illinois (U of I).

evidence.title: University of Illinois round barns
evidence.text: The University of Illinois was home to one of the Agricultural Experiment Stations, located at U.S. universities, which were at the heart of the promotion of the round barn.

evidence.title: University of Illinois round barns
evidence.text: At least one round barn in Illinois was built specifically after its owner viewed the barns at the university.

evidence.title: University of Illinois round barns
evidence.text: Though originally an experiment the three barns helped to lead the way for round barn construction throughout the Midwest, particularly in Illinois.

evidence.title: University of Illinois round barns
evidence.text: The barns were listed as contributing properties to the U of I Experimental Dairy Farm Historic District, which was listed on the U.S. National Register of Historic Places in 1994.

evidence.title: Dammon Round Barn
evidence.text: Dammon Round Barn is a round barn just southeast of Red Wing, Minnesota, United States, adjacent to U.S. Route 61.

evidence.title: Dammon Round Barn
evidence.text: The barn is listed on the National Register of Historic Places.

evidence.title: Dammon Round Barn
evidence.text: It was built in 1914, with a foundation of Mississippi River limestone, and is 60 ft in diameter and 60 ft high.

evidence.title: Dammon Round Barn
evidence.text: It was built during a time of agricultural growth in Goodhue County, when dairy cow herds were averaging 25 cows per farm and farmers were starting to build specialized barns.

evidence.title: Dammon Round Barn
evidence.text: The round barn design was built around a silo and provided insulation for the silage, as well as making feeding and cleaning easier.

evidence.title: Dammon Round Barn
evidence.text: Despite the efficiency, however, round barns were difficult to construct, and they were not widely adopted.

evidence.title: Dammon Round Barn
evidence.text: Later in its history the barn was used for honey production of the bee keeping owners of the farm.

evidence.title: Dammon Round Barn
evidence.text: In 2000 the Farm was purchased by Robin and Elaine Kleffman and the Dammon Barn underwent some significant restoration.

evidence.title: Dammon Round Barn
evidence.text: A straightening of the walls and replacement of the original pillars for the upper floor support and a leveling and new installation of a floor in the top level of the barn makes this one of the most premiere remaining round barns in Minnesota.
